- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates — apply downward bias of 2–5% to forecast mean.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — delay forecast correction by 1–2 periods.
- If true outcome consistently underperforms model (e.g., 3+ consecutive under-forecasts), apply mean reversion: next forecast = prior true + 0.5×(prior forecast - prior true).
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — reduce forecast by 3–5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., < -0.3 for 5+ days), model tends to underestimate — add 2–4% to forecast mean to compensate.
